generic_domain.justification:
The term 'optimization' is the broadest and most encompassing category in the given list. It refers to a general process of finding the best solution or alternative from all feasible solutions, which can be applied across various contexts such as engineering, economics, and computer science. The other domains listed are specific types of optimization methods or scenarios:

definitions-Adjustable Optimization: This involves optimizing systems that can be adjusted over time or in response to changing conditions.
definitions-Constrained Optimization: Focuses on finding optimal solutions under certain constraints or restrictions.
definitions-Continuous Optimization and Discrete Optimization: These deal with problems where the variables are continuous (can take any value within a range) or discrete (only specific, distinct values). Both fall under the broader category of optimization.\n\n    The term 'optimization' does not exclude any of these sub-domains. Instead, it serves as an umbrella term that includes all of them, making it the most generic and comprehensive domain in this list.
